fix(test): expect docx kind from office file reader

Align unit test with UI kind discrimination (docx|xlsx|pptx) so Windows/macOS CI cargo test passes.

docs: replace README screenshots with product captures [skip ci]

Use real macOS UI shots (workbench, account, light theme, chat/media)
instead of structural placeholders; compressed for GitHub display.

Adopt community PR: session auto-title LLM prompt follows settings.locale (en/zh). Strips English Title: prefix. Closes feedback from @Sdefendre about hard-coded Chinese titles.

Co-authored-by: Steve Defendre <steve.defendre12@gmail.com>

fix: use Grok Build permission optionIds (underscore)

Adopt community PR: shell tool permission fallbacks must use allow_once/reject (underscore), not hyphenated ACP ids. Fixes failed permission / stuck turns when running terminal tools.

Co-authored-by: Steve Defendre <steve.defendre12@gmail.com>

- Allow drafting while streaming so stalled turns do not hard-lock the input.
- Single-instance plugin focuses existing window (Dock multi-open).
- Titlebar: safer mac traffic-light inset; panel toggle non-drag.
- docs/llm-wiki/maintain.md + labels/issues #3–#13 from launch X feedback.

Fixes #9. Fixes #4 (draft unlock). Fixes #7. Partial #8.

fix: session history dedupe, thinking collapse, clearer agent errors

- Stream chunks only bind to the current turn (after last user); adopt host
  messageId on optimistic pending; clear stuck streaming on send and turn end.
- Journal append_message upserts by id; stronger history-bootstrap anti-echo.
- Thinking/reasoning auto-collapse when done; remember expand preference.
- Add QUOTA_EXCEEDED / CONNECT_FAILED codes; map connect/quota/auth phrases;
  clearer login Access denied message.

Fixes #3. Fixes #10. Fixes #6. Improves #5.

feat: multi-account, chat import, login UX, Linux packaging

- Multi-account: save/switch/remove auth snapshots under app data;
  auto-snapshot after login; Settings → Account switcher.
- Login: longer poll, device URL auto-open, Access denied help copy + UI tips.
- Import conversation from markdown/JSON file as local session (web history
  is not available via Grok Build CLI).
- Linux: build:linux script, CI rust job, release matrix ubuntu-22.04,
  docs and platform badges.

Closes #5, #11, #12, #13.

ui: hide multi-account and import-chat sections for now

Gate Settings → Account extras behind SHOW_ACCOUNT_EXTRAS=false so the
product surface stays login/quota only. Backend APIs remain for later.

fix: plan exit_plan_mode + split multi-phase thinking (minos-aligned)

- Handle _x.ai/exit_plan_mode with planContent body; reply approved/
  cancelled/abandoned so Approve & build actually unblocks the agent.
- Wire Plan card Approve / Request changes / Dismiss actions.
- Thought chunks bind to current assistant messageId; split pre-tool vs
  post-tool reasoning into separate UI thinking blocks (not one blob).

Closes #15. Closes #16.

fix: allow binding orphan sessions to a project folder

Composer project chip is now a menu: pick a trusted project or clear to
orphan. Host persists session.projectId via session_set_project and drops
live ACP so the next send reconnects under the new cwd.

Closes #14.

fix: session data mode switch + plan approve buttons

Settings → Session data mode used window.confirm when switching to
shared mode; Tauri WebView often returns false with no dialog, so the
control appeared stuck. Use in-app setAppDialog confirm instead.

Plan card could lose exit_plan_mode rpcId when a later sessionUpdate
plan notification arrived without one, which disabled Approve /
Request changes and left only Dismiss working. Preserve pending
rpcId/toolCallId across updates.

Fixes #19. Fixes #17.

feat(i18n): add Traditional Chinese (zh-TW) locale (#18)

Thanks @jason920612!

Adds 繁體中文 (Taiwan terminology) as a third UI locale with full key parity, tray strings, Settings selector, and docs.

Verified: merge onto main → tsc clean, vitest 172/172.

feat(acp): API mode — connect to a remote ACP server over TCP (#20)

Thanks @jason920612!

Optional API mode: connect to a remote ACP server over TCP (host:port) instead of spawning local \`grok agent stdio\`. Empty setting keeps the previous local spawn path.

Verified: merge onto main (post #18) is clean for Rust/FE; cargo check clean. Follow-up commit will add the new i18n keys to zh-TW.

fix: zh-TW ACP keys + remove remaining window.confirm

- Add settings.acpServer / settings.acpServerDesc to zh-TW after PR #20.
- Replace project-trust window.confirm after add-project with setAppDialog
  (same Tauri WebView reliability issue as session data mode).

Keeps Locale key parity and dialogs.md policy.

fix: allow canceling a stuck login (OAuth/device) mid-flight

Previously, clicking a sign-in method set a "working" state that blocked
all controls until the grok login CLI returned. OAuth waits on a browser
callback and device-code flow polls a verification URL, so this could take
minutes or never resolve — leaving the only escape as quitting the app.

Now the backend spawns the CLI via tokio::process and races its completion
against a cancel notifier (Notify); Cancel kills the child, the pending
handler's finally clears accountBusy, and the user can pick another method.

- account.rs: LoginProcState (OnceLock global), async spawn + select, cancel
- commands.rs / lib.rs: account_login_cancel command
- api.ts: accountLoginCancel()
- SetupWizard + AccountPanel: Cancel button while busy
- i18n: setup.account.cancelBusy / account.loginCancel (en + zh + zh-TW)

Unblocks cargo after zh-TW locale was added to tray_i18n::Locale.

Stop resolving settings copy via App's partial labels whitelist — missing
keys rendered as raw strings (e.g. settings.acpServer). Prefer createT(locale)
for all SettingsPage t() lookups, including ACP test field vars.
docs(i18n): ban partial labels whitelist for settings copy

build: Windows portable zip, Linux deb/rpm, release download table

Wire package-windows-portable.sh in release CI; expand bundle targets
to dmg/nsis/appimage/deb/rpm; document green-zip and Linux packages in

feat: integrate PRs #25–#27 (context chip, Extensions, docs)

Absorb community context usage chip and Settings → Extensions Skills/MCP
manager onto main multi-account workbench; wire i18n + CSS; OAuth browser
open already landed with packaging. Docs for Extensions surfaces.

Track agent write/edit tool events in the active session and surface them
in ResourceViewer as a Changes list with optional unified diff (tool

Add full rewind timeline and session fork UX on top of existing ACP

- Pure helpers + tests for truncate/fork; i18n en/zh/zh-TW

Cap warm agent processes (default 3) with park/unpark by session, reject
or recycle LRU when over capacity, and soft-kill idle Ready agents after

feat: surface ask_user_question with in-app questionnaire UI

Wire `_x.ai/ask_user_question` through AcpClient → session://ask_user →
GlassModal so agents can collect option/free-text answers instead of

unit tests, and en/zh/zh-TW strings.

merge: integrate PR #28 session changes / diff panel

Resource pane Files|Changes, tool before/after snippets, optional

merge: integrate PR #29 session fork and rewind timeline

execute; ConversationThread hover rewind.

merge: integrate PR #30 agent process limits and idle recycle

Concurrent agent cap + idle recycle settings; keep AcpServerField test UI
and bilingual process-limit toasts.

merge: integrate PR #31 ask_user_question in-app UI

Parse ACP ask_user events, AskUserModal answers/cancel, keep process
limits last_activity and shortcuts modal.

Document session Changes, fork/rewind, process limits, and ask-user UI.

Community fix: gate live stream emission on FSM Streaming|AwaitingPermission so session/load transcript replay is not re-typed as a live turn. Host + frontend defense-in-depth.

Reviewed: clear root cause, CI green (frontend + Rust macOS/Windows/Linux), no i18n/dialogs/secrets issues.

T06: extract pure wire_*/decode_* helpers and lock ACP shapes with offline golden fixtures under tests/fixtures/acp/.

Reviewed: CI green, no UI/i18n, protocol regression suite only (behavior preserved via pure extract).

Reviewed: CI green, no new user-facing strings, short lists unchanged, no drive-by refactors beyond list wiring.

L03: Extensions enable toggles, inject enabled MCP into ACP session/new|load, dual-write agent-home config, soft-respawn on change.

Reviewed: CI green; i18n en/zh/zh-TW; default-on opt-out model accepted by maintainer.

Service via keyring, with secrets.json 0600 fallback and one-time
plaintext migration. load_secrets/save_secrets API unchanged.

Community PR #34 (sonnemusk).

Host watchdog emits session://stream_stall after pure silence (default
120s); Cancel turn / Keep waiting UI. Mid-stream journal flushes ≥500ms
or on paragraph / turn end. Keeps #35 resume-stream drop guard.

Community PR #37 (sonnemusk).

Session + Workspace sections: git status porcelain, unified diff via
git_file_diff / git_show_file, soft-fail when git/repo missing. No discard.

Community PR #36 (sonnemusk).

Community PR #39 (sonnemusk).

Queue messages when the agent is streaming/connecting; auto-flush after

Community PR #40 (tisrop).

Community follow-ups after X launch feedback:

Plan review in resources; top progress only; no thread plan card.

Opt-in OS keychain; startup no longer probes Keychain on cold launch.

Sidebar shows custom provider when active; aggregate local usage for agent-home sessions.

Plan resource review, top-only progress, keychain opt-in, custom provider

feat: switch git worktrees from the project chip (#46)

List linked worktrees for the active project (git worktree list) and
switch the session cwd by selecting one. Reuses an existing project when
the path matches; otherwise adds the folder (trust inherited when possible).

feat: project-level permission tiers for trusted folders (#47)

Trusted projects can pin a permission default (Ask / Accept edits / session
/ Deny / Full access) that overrides the app-wide default. Untrusted projects
always force Ask so a stored relaxed tier cannot apply before trust. Cascade
is session → project → global and feeds the existing Host policy + scope_key
path. Set or clear the tier from the project context menu; YOLO still uses
the two-step in-app confirm.

feat: edit and save text files in the resource pane (#50)

Text/code/markdown tabs can be edited in-pane with dirty state, Save
(⌘/Ctrl+S), and Revert. Write goes through fs_write_file under the
project root (or absolute path when opened that way) with mtime-based
conflict detection so agent/external overwrites are not silent.
Markdown stays in preview until Edit; closing a dirty tab asks first.

fix(composer): restore image paste on Tauri / macOS screenshots (#48)

WebView paste events often have no File objects for screenshots, so the
old path silently did nothing after preventDefault. Try clipboard event
Files first, then async Clipboard API, then native OS clipboard (arboard
→ PNG under attachments/paste). Show attach toast on success and a clear
error when media paste fails. + menu file picker also confirms attach.

feat: structured error deck for CLI/auth/network/crash (#51)

Map host error codes to problem + cause + primary/secondary actions
(open Doctor, set CLI path, account, reconnect, etc.) and show them on
the workbench banner. Copy lives in i18n (en/zh/zh-TW); local UX strings
stay plain with a dismiss action.

docs: refresh features, contributors, and Unreleased changelog

Document merged community work (#46–#51): worktree switch, project
permission tiers, image paste, resource edit, error deck. Expand README
feature tables (zh/en) and name community contributors with highlights.

Move Unreleased notes (worktree, permission tiers, resource edit,
clipboard paste, error deck) into the 0.1.5 section for release-tag.
chore: release v0.1.5

fix(ui): stop Git worktrees menu text flicker

Open-effect depended on an inline onOpen that changed every parent
render, so the menu re-fetched in a loop and swapped loading/empty
copy. Call onOpen only when the menu opens, soft-refresh without
blanking an existing list, and use a real loading label.

fix: do not end turns while tools or permission are still open

Agents often emit prompt_complete before tools finish or while the host
is waiting on permission / plan / ask_user. Ending the UI turn then looks
like the request was cut off mid-task (#52). Defer end_stream until tools
settle and gates clear. Also toast when sending in agent mode without a
project folder so write work has a workspace.

fix(ui): hide non-git worktrees and compact worktree rows

Only show the GIT WORKTREES block after host confirms a git work tree
(no loading placeholder for ordinary folders). Match project-row height
with a single-line branch + badge layout.

fix(session): diagnostic export, HOME cwd for orphans, empty-run toast

Help triage early end_turn reports (#52): session menu exports a redacted
diagnostic zip; no-project agents use $HOME instead of Dock cwd `/`;
soft toast when a non-ask turn ends with zero tool calls.

feat: import Grok Build CLI sessions in shared mode

When session data mode is shared (~/.grok), Settings lists CLI sessions
from GROK_HOME/sessions and can import chat_history.jsonl into the app
sidebar. Already-linked agent ids are marked; import is one-shot or bulk.

fix: lock store JSON writes against concurrent corruption (#55)

Shared mode (and dual App instances) can tear sessions_index / messages
mid-write. Write through an exclusive sidecar lock with temp+rename, and
quarantine corrupt index/message JSON instead of silent empty parse.

feat: a11y for streaming, permission bar, and ask_user (#53)

Announce stream start/end once for screen readers (not every token).
Permission bar is a modal dialog with focus on Allow, Tab trap, and
Escape → deny. GlassModal restores focus and traps Tab. Ask-user
options expose pressed state and group labels. Conversation log uses
aria-live polite.

feat: keep busy sessions streaming after switching chats (#56)

Previously switching away from a streaming session was blocked. Busy
live sessions demote to a background map, keep receiving ACP events
(stream/tools/permission), and promote back when re-focused. Idle Ready
sessions still park as before. Background permission shows a toast +
desktop notify so approvals do not attach to the wrong chat.

fix(session): merge #54 turn-complete defer with empty-run signal

Keep prompt_complete deferred while tools/permission/plan/ask_user are
open (issue #52) and preserve empty-run soft toast when a finished turn
had zero tool calls. Resolve conflicts with diagnostic export / HOME cwd.

Record multi-session stream, a11y, deferred turn-complete, store lock,
and community issue closures on the post-0.1.5 board.

Merge origin/main into shared-cli-sessions

Resolve lib.rs module list: keep cli_sessions with turn_complete and store_lock.

docs: refresh README features and contributor avatars

Re-fetch GitHub contributors; show avatar wall + table with commits and
highlights. Sync feature tables for multi-session stream, CLI import,
diagnostics, and store locks (zh + en).

feat: check for App updates from GitHub Releases (#58)

Settings → About can query the latest release, compare semver, and open
the release page. Installers stay manual — no silent Tauri updater until
signing keys land in CI.

feat: show active agent tool tasks in the right pane (#59)

Derive a Tasks list from live ACP tool_step / session://tool events
already tracked in the session stream (title, kind, status, detail).
No separate ACP task API and no fake per-tool Kill — status only.

feat: search session message content from palette (#60)

Sidebar search was title/project only. Scan App journal messages.json
for case-insensitive substrings, return snippet + match count, and show
content hits under titles with debounced host search.

feat: install and update plugins from Settings → Extensions (#61)

Wrap `grok plugin install` (path / git URL / owner/repo, with --trust)
and `plugin update` (one or all). Soft-respawn after success, surface
CLI-missing like the rest of the panel, and keep en/zh/zh-TW in sync.

fix: recycle agents when session_data_mode changes (#62)

Switching independent↔shared changes GROK_HOME. Kill live, background,
and parked agents so none keep the old home; clear live agentSessionId
so reconnect uses session/new + journal bootstrap. Toast on recycle.
Import still never forces shared mode (E05). Shared confirm dialog kept.

feat: relocate missing project folders (pathOk UX) (#65)

* feat: relocate missing project folders (pathOk UX)

When Host marks pathOk false (folder deleted/moved), show a sidebar badge
and composer chip warning, offer Relocate… (pick dir → project_relocate),
and block agent connect/send until the path is a real directory again.

* test: serialize project store integration tests

Parallel cargo test workers share projects.json; lock so relocate
does not lose its row under concurrent add/remove (macOS CI flake).

feat: sandbox profile setting for agent spawn (#66)

Add AppSettings.sandbox_profile (default off) and pass it to the
Grok Build CLI as top-level --sandbox / GROK_SANDBOX when spawning
agent stdio. Settings → Permissions exposes the built-in profiles.

feat: pin sessions to top of sidebar (#73)

Sessions get a pinned flag (default false) and sort pinned-first
then by updated_at, matching project pin behavior. Context menu and
hover control pin/unpin; pinned rows show a pin icon.

feat: project inspect panel in Settings → Runtime (#75)

Expose a secret-safe summary of `grok inspect --json` for the active
workbench project: plugins, skills, MCP, rules paths, and model hints.
Supports refresh, copy redacted JSON, and reveal of project `.grok`.

feat: merge grok doctor --json into App Doctor (#76)

Run the probed CLI `doctor --json` during doctor_report (15s timeout)
and surface findings as pass/warn/fail rows under a dedicated section.
Safe environment facts (terminal, clipboard, color, …) stay in a
collapsible block. Pure TS parser has a unit-test fixture; en/zh/zh-TW.

docs: CHANGELOG for merged PR batch #58–#76 (partial)

Record App update, tasks panel, content search, plugin install, sandbox,
session pin, project inspect, CLI doctor, mode recycle, and pathOk relocate.
Note remaining open PRs blocked by conflicts.

feat: English-first open source defaults and live voice workbench

Make English the product default for open-source distribution: settings
locale, App bootstrap, resolveLocale, tray fallback, and dialog titles.
README is English-primary (Chinese retained as README_ZH).

Add Live Voice foundation for GPT-Live-style agent delegation:
dictation (xAI STT), live voice host (realtime WS + host tools),
VoiceOverlay UI, mock mode (GROK_APP_VOICE=mock), and unit tests.

feat: Settings → Keyboard shortcuts (read-only catalog)

Add a dedicated settings section that lists shipped keybindings from the
same SHORTCUTS catalog as the help modal. Grouped table shows macOS and
Windows/Linux chords; current platform column is highlighted. Remapping
is intentionally not included yet.

feat: voice dictation into the composer

Replace the voice-soon placeholder with a working mic control: capture
audio in the WebView, transcribe via xAI STT (official OAuth/API key),
and insert text into the draft. Ctrl+Space toggles; Esc cancels. Relay-only
auth stays disabled with an actionable message. macOS mic usage string included.

fix(voice): caret insert, cancel STT, auth class, 10s silence stop

- Capture caret offset before stop and insert at that index
- Bump generation on cancel so in-flight STT never mutates draft
- Trust Host errorClass tokens (auth/no_speech/…) in classify path
- Arm VOICE_NO_SPEECH_MS timer while recording (fail-closed no_speech)

fix(voice): auto-stop runs STT instead of discarding speech

The 10s timer no longer cancel()s capture into forced no_speech. Cap is
60s via stop()+transcribe; no_speech only when STT/tiny blob is empty.

feat: check and install Grok Build CLI updates

Settings → Runtime and Doctor can run `grok update --check --json`, show
current/latest status, and install when available. Install prefers the
resolved CLI's own `grok update` (channel-aware), with fallback to the
App install trust-chain. Parse path is unit-tested without network.

feat: git worktree garbage collect (prune) from project chip

Add git_worktree_gc host command wrapping `git worktree prune` with
safe argv only (dry-run, optional force → --expire now, optional max-age).
Project chip offers “Clean stale worktrees…” with GlassModal dry-run
preview then apply; refreshes the worktree list after.

- Pure arg builders + unit tests (Rust + TS)
- i18n en / zh / zh-TW
- Docs + CHANGELOG Unreleased

ci: trigger GitHub Actions on open PR

Checks did not start after initial push.

feat: apply CLI doctor automatic remediations from App Doctor

Parse automaticRemediation / fixId from doctor JSON, invoke
`grok doctor fix <id> --yes` via cli_doctor_fix (timeout, redacted
stdout/stderr), and show Apply fix on DoctorModal rows. Destructive
fixes use the in-app confirm dialog; doctor re-runs after apply.
Pure extractFixIds helper + fixture tests; en/zh/zh-TW.

feat: find in current conversation (Cmd/Ctrl+F)

Sidebar/palette search is cross-session. Add an in-chat find bar so
users can jump matches inside the open transcript: case-insensitive
query over user + assistant text, prev/next, match count, highlight
and scroll into view. Escape closes; composer typing stays intact
when the bar is closed.

feat: experimental cross-session memory toggle and clear

Add settings.experimentalMemory (default off) so App can enable Grok Build
cross-session memory via --experimental-memory / GROK_MEMORY=1 and independent
agent-home [memory] enabled. When off, spawn forces --no-memory + GROK_MEMORY=0
for isolation. Settings UI includes an in-app confirm to run grok memory clear
for the current project workspace. Pure flag/env helpers covered by vitest.

feat: MCP add/remove/doctor in Extensions

Settings → Extensions can add stdio MCP servers, remove with in-app
confirm, and run grok mcp doctor. Config writes respect session_data_mode
GROK_HOME; live agent soft-respawns after add/remove.

feat: max agent turns setting for agent spawn

Add AppSettings.max_agent_turns (optional; None/0 omit the flag) and pass
top-level --max-turns N when spawning grok agent stdio. Settings → Runtime
exposes a 0–200 number input (empty/0 = CLI default). Clamp + CLI arg
builder covered by unit tests.

feat: disable web search/fetch for agents via settings

Add AppSettings.disable_web_search (default false). When on, agent
spawn passes top-level --disable-web-search so web_search and
web_fetch are removed. Toggle lives under Settings → Permissions;
flipping soft-respawns live agents. Unit tests cover spawn flags
and serde default for older settings files.

feat: reopen last chat on startup

Two issues in src-tauri/src/session_title.rs:

fix(i18n): accept case/alias variants of locale ids in resolveLocale

resolveLocale used isLocale for an exact string match, so a settings value
that was hand-edited to a differently-cased or aliased id (e.g. "zh-tw",
"zh_Hant", "EN-US") failed the guard and silently fell back to the product
default. The Rust side (tray_i18n.rs Locale::parse) already parses these
case-insensitively, so the tray and auto-titles could render Traditional
while the web UI stayed on the fallback locale.

Add a normalizeLocale() step inside resolveLocale that lowercases/trims and
maps the same reasonable variants to the canonical Locale union value. The
isLocale type guard is left as an exact check so canonical values keep their
fast path and the guard stays honest; the stored canonical value written by
the settings UI is unchanged.

zh-tw / zh_TW / zh-Hant, simplified/English aliases, and unknown/empty
falling back to the default.

feat(mirror): loopback HTTP+WS host to drive the workbench from a phone

Add an optional "phone mirror" host: a token-gated loopback HTTP + WebSocket
server that serves the existing SPA to a phone browser and bridges it to the
running desktop session. Off by default and zero-cost until the user starts it.

Rust module `src/mirror/`:
- http.rs  — axum server bound to 127.0.0.1 only; every route gated by a
             `/t/{token}/` path prefix (constant-time token compare, fail-closed
             401); serves the SPA shell with an injected <base href> + token, and
             hashed /assets/* for code-split chunks.
- ws.rs    — per-connection WebSocket hub: JSON-RPC in, event fan-out out.
- rpc.rs   — explicit command allowlist (the security boundary). Only the
             methods a phone needs are reachable; desktop-only surfaces
             (file pickers, editor open, CLI install, account login, reset,
             fs browse) return UNSUPPORTED. Includes stateless composer voice
             dictation (voice.status / voice.transcribe) reusing the same xAI
             STT call the desktop uses.
- tunnel.rs— optional cloudflared quick tunnel spawned in its own process group
             (killed cleanly on stop/exit); local-only mode needs no tunnel.
- auth.rs  — 32-byte URL-safe token generation + constant-time comparison.

Host wiring in lib.rs: register `MirrorHost` state, add mirror_status/start/stop
commands, optional headless autostart (GROK_MIRROR_HEADLESS), and teardown on
app exit.

Event fan-out (the one invasive change): `session://*` emits in session_manager
now go through `mirror::fanout_event`, which calls `app.emit` exactly as before
and additionally broadcasts to any connected mirror clients. Desktop behaviour is
unchanged when no mirror client is connected.

Config via env (all optional): GROK_MIRROR_HEADLESS, GROK_MIRROR_TOKEN,
GROK_MIRROR_PORT, GROK_MIRROR_NO_TUNNEL, GROK_MIRROR_DIST.

Deps: axum, tower, tower-http, rand.

fix(acp): stop the prompt_complete fallback from truncating live turns

Agents fire `_x.ai/session/prompt_complete` before the answer is finished.
The fallback armed by that notification slept a flat 3s and then resolved the
pending `session/prompt` with a synthetic result, which surfaced as an
`authoritative: true` completion while chunks were still arriving. The turn
closed, `prompt_in_flight` went false, and every later chunk was discarded by
the replay guard — journal keeps a clean prefix, UI freezes mid-sentence,
agent side reports `turn_ended outcome=completed`, no error anywhere.

Session 9019d19a: agent wrote 2380 chars, journal kept 1528 (last write
09:27:32.31, agent streamed until 09:27:40.20). This defeated the R11 fix
from the inside: R11.2 requires only the RPC result to end a turn, and the
fallback was forging one.

The window is now idle-based — each inbound `session/update` re-arms it, so
the waiter is released only after the agent actually goes quiet.
`PROMPT_TIMEOUT_SECS` stays the backstop for a wedged RPC.

Also warn instead of silently dropping a background chunk that arrives after
its turn closed: a background chat never replays `session/load`, so that path
is always real output loss.

fix(session): stop sidebar stuck-busy after settled turns (#225)

Root cause for multi-turn “executing forever” with no visible progress:

1. Late/coalesced stream tokens re-projected liveMap to `streaming` after the
   host had already settled the turn to ready (especially background chats
   where anti-replay does not drop tokens).
2. `turn_empty_run`, `stream_stall_hard_end`, and `idle_recycled` only toasted
   and never settled client liveMap when stream `done` was missed.

Gate stream busy promotions with mayPromoteStreamingFromStreamChunk and settle
liveMap (and viewed workbench) on empty-run / hard-stall / idle recycle.

Helpers + tests live in permissionRules.ts; i18n en/zh/zh-TW + CHANGELOG.

Host live slot. Re-open focuses the existing window; secondary close

`--remote <URL>`, masked client CLI string (`grok --remote ws://… --secret …`),
one-time full copy on start, and a health note that only probes local bind TCP.

JSON stdin, timeout, and redacted stdout/stderr. Refuse paths outside

ExtensionsHooksPanel for Settings → Extensions → Hooks (list + Try +

SessionMeta.forkAgentSession so next connect uses ACP session/fork

Add buildExportImagePipeline e2e that rasterizes real PNG via node-canvas.

feat(ui): flat session list, JSON Schema in + menu, theme flyout

fix(chat): invalidate export preview on smart-mode toggle

Clear blob/URL and force busy whenever the export preview rebuilds so

fix: evict detached sessions so reload skips the CLI 5s thread drain

The CLI's session/load waits up to 5s for the old session thread to finish
before replaying the same session (drain_old_session_thread). App detach
(return to prewarm / shared keep) left the actor resident, so reloading the
same history chat cost a fixed 5s. Now detach issues x.ai/internal/evict_sessions
(fire-and-forget): the CLI unloads the idle actor to disk WITHOUT finalizing
the cloud replica (still resumable), so the next load finishes immediately.
Kill path skips evict (process death cleans up).

fix: refresh prewarm after every reuse (clean CLI, no 5s reload drain)

The CLI accumulates a session actor per session/load and has NO public unload
API (x.ai/internal/evict_sessions is leader-internal → Method not found;
session/close finalizes the cloud replica). So a reused process reloading the
same session waits the CLI's 5s old-thread drain (drain_old_session_thread).

Fix: every warm-process reuse now spawns prewarm_force — a fresh clean CLI —
so the next session/load always happens on a process that never loaded that
session (no old thread → fast). connect waits up to 2.5s for a Spawning
prewarm before falling back. Viewed-only detach kills its exclusive process
(clears actors); the prewarm slot is refreshed on the next connect.

PrewarmState: None | Spawning{since} | Ready(process); prewarm_inner runs
outside connect_lock (connect may await a Spawning prewarm — holding the lock
there would deadlock).

fix: retire old prewarm process on force refresh (no leak)

prewarm_force replaced the prewarm slot without killing the previous Ready
process — every reuse refreshed the slot and leaked a CLI process. Now the
old process is killed (async) before the fresh one spawns.

fix(tool-timeline): capture ACP output, fix tool identity, free plan mode

Three coupled defects behind "tool rows show bare 工具 and can't expand" plus
the plan-mode trap, all verified against real session journals before fixing.

1. Tool output was never captured.
   extract_tool_ui_fields only read rawInput (command/query/description), so
   `detail` was the *call argument* echoed back — never the result. read_file /
   grep / list tools produced no expandable body at all (hasBody=false → the
   row rendered as a <span>, not a clickable <button>). Add extract_tool_output
   that reads ACP content[] (text items + diff headers), emit it on
   session://tool, persist it behind a sentinel so the legacy
   tool_step| body parses byte-identically, and render it as a terminal-style
   boxed block (command echoed above output) shared by both row types.

2. Machine tool name was unreachable.
   The _meta key is literally "x.ai/tool"; JSON Pointer requires the inner
   slash to be escaped as ~1 (RFC 6901). `/_meta/x.ai/tool/name` never
   resolved, so on sparse terminal updates the journal collapsed to
   `tool_step|failed|tool|tool`. Add tool_meta()/tool_meta_str() helpers and
   fix the two call sites (session_manager types + acp_client permission).

3. Plan mode could not be cancelled.
   `mode: "plan"` was persisted into global settings (and project defaults),
   so every new session inherited it; and PlanStatusBar rendered no exit
   control for kind==="plan_mode". Plan mode is transient/per-session: drop it
   at every global/project persistence site (sticky_mode), heal the value
   already on disk (non_plan_mode), and give the idle plan chip a close
   button that flips back to agent.

plan-mode healing/stickiness), +5 TS (output expand body, read-file
expandability, long-output elision, sentinel parser, output threading +
survives sparse tick). Full suite: 5065 TS + 1104 Rust green (2 pre-existing

fix: per-chat turn/gate clocks and reasoning effort; discoverable bulk select; per-provider appended prompt (#595)

* fix(session): keep turn and gate clocks per chat

The "thinking for N" timer, the tool-permission auto-deny countdown and the
ask-user auto-cancel all restarted whenever the user left a chat and came
back. Each read its start time from the wrong place:

- The turn clock lived in one global `turnStartedAt`. Of the five writers,
  only the `session://state` "turn ended" branch skipped the check for which
  chat the event belonged to, so a *background* chat going idle stopped the
  clock of the chat on screen. Reopening a chat mid-turn then had nothing to
  restore from and started over at zero.
- Both gate countdowns anchored to the moment their UI mounted. "New chat"
  clears the pending request and so does switching chats, so every return
  granted a fresh full timeout and the deadline never arrived.

Keep the turn clock per session (`turnStartedAtBySessionRef`, mirrored into
the visible timer, restored by `openSession`) with explicit start/restart/
clear helpers, and give the event handlers the session they are acting on.
Resume gate countdowns from a clock keyed to the request via the new shared
`lib/gateClock`, dropping it once the request is answered or expires.

Refs: session://state, session://interjection, turn markers

* fix(prefs): remember reasoning effort per chat

Raising effort in one conversation silently changed every other one. The
memory scope setting is labelled "model & permission", but effort followed
it too, and its default is global — so a single `settings.effort` backed
every chat. Chats that had picked their own effort (`max`, `low`) were all
displayed and spawned as the newest global value.

Cascade effort session → project → global the way permission already does,
independent of `composer_prefs_scope`; `settings.effort` is now only the
seed for chats that never chose one. `save_composer_prefs` writes it onto
the session row under any scope.

A draft chat made this worse: with `sessionId: null` the command fell back
to the live session id, so changing effort before the first message wrote
it into whichever conversation was still running and soft-respawned that
agent. Keep the draft's `None` (it seeds the global default instead), and
gate `set_effort_and_respawn_needed` on the change actually belonging to
the live slot.

* feat(sidebar): make bulk select discoverable

Multi-select, group select-all, Shift-range and the archive/delete action
bar all existed, but the only way to turn the mode on was a hover-only icon
on the **Projects** group header. Chats that belong to no project live under
**Other chats**, so users whose sidebar looks like that — including anyone
with no projects configured at all — had no reachable entry point.

Add the two paths people actually reach for:

- Session context menu → **Select**, which enters the mode with that chat
  already ticked and anchored, so Shift-clicking another row selects the
  range immediately. Hidden while the mode is on, where it would otherwise
  clear the current selection.
- The **Other chats** header gets the same hover action the Projects header
  already had; `.tree-l1__actions` styling already covers it.

* feat(providers): per-channel appended prompt

Some relays need instructions of their own (response language, tool syntax,
refusal style) that do not belong in every chat. Add an **Appended prompt**
box to the provider editor, empty by default.

It rides the CLI's `--rules` flag, which appends to the system prompt —
`--system-prompt-override` would replace it and cost the agent its built-in
behaviour. `merge_extra_rules` folds the active channel's text in next to
the session's own rules at connect, so the official route is untouched.

Stored per channel in agent-home `config.toml` as `app_append_prompt`,
following the existing `app_*` convention for fields Grok Build ignores.
Values are JSON-quoted, so multi-line text survives the line-based parser;
an emptied box clears the field, while an edit that omits it keeps what is
on disk rather than silently wiping it.

test(win): read source files as LF before asserting on them (#730)

`window-config.test.ts` asserts that `tray.rs` contains
`…&AppHandle) {\n    hide_to_tray_inner(app, false);`. The repo stores LF, but
git's default `core.autocrlf=true` on Windows writes CRLF into the working
tree, so the file on disk has `\r\n` and the assertion fails against source
that is perfectly correct.

It fails for Windows contributors only, which is the worst kind of red: CI is
green, the source is right, and a first-time contributor has to work out that
the failure is about their git config.

Read through a small `readSource` helper that normalizes to LF. The other two
source reads in the file (`win_shell.rs`, `Cargo.toml`) go through it too — they
only use `toMatch` today, but the next `\n` in an expectation should not
reintroduce this.

A repo-level `.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf` would prevent the CRLF
from ever reaching the working tree in the first place. I left that out
deliberately: it is a repo-wide policy call that rewrites every Windows
contributor's checkout, and it belongs to you, not to a test fix. The helper
also covers checkouts made before such a file would exist, and source archives.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

i18n(de): a turn is a Vorgang, not a Zug (#728)

The German catalog renders the agent **turn** as "Zug" in 125 places. In
German a `Zug` is a train, or a move in chess. It is never a unit of work, so
`account.col.turns` is a table column headed *Trains* and
`notify.turnDoneTitle` says *Grok completed a chess move*.

"Vorgang" — an operation, a process — is masculine exactly like `Zug`, so
every surrounding article and case ending stays correct with no further edits:
`dieser Zug` → `dieser Vorgang`, `des Zugs` → `des Vorgangs`, `den Zügen` →
`den Vorgängen`. That gender match is why not `Runde` or `Antwort` (both
feminine): either would mean touching the words around all 125 sites, and each
of those is a chance to introduce a new mistake.

Compounds follow: `Agentenzug` → `Agentenvorgang`, `Zugende` → `Vorgangsende`,
`Zug-Limits` → `Vorgangs-Limits`. `Mitten-im-Zug-Hinweise` becomes
`Mitten-im-Vorgang-Hinweise` and keeps no linking -s: the head sits inside a
frozen prepositional phrase.

Untouched: ordinary German words that merely contain the letters and mean
something else — `Zugriff` and its compounds, `bevorzugen`, `hinzugefügt`,
`freizugeben`, `zugehörig`, `einzugreifen`, `Auszug` / `Auszüge`. The pass
asserts nothing outside that list survives.

fix(i18n): three bugs the 15-locale rollout activated (#726)

* fix(title): peel quotes by character so CJK titles stop panicking

`clean_llm_title` stripped a surrounding quote pair with
`t[1..t.len() - 1]`. `「」` and `“”` are three bytes each, so that slice
cut a codepoint in half and panicked — and those are exactly the quotes a
title model puts around Japanese and Chinese output.
`refine_title_in_background` swallows the panic, so auto-titling just
stopped silently and the session kept its heuristic name.

The 120-unit sanity cap counted bytes as well, which is only 40 Japanese
characters: a title was rejected at a length its English equivalent
passed. Both now count characters.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(title): recognise every shipped locale's placeholder name

The app writes `session.placeholderTitle` to disk in the user's language,
so a German session is stored as "Neuer Chat" and a Korean one as
"새 대화". `is_placeholder_title` matched a hand-kept list of English and
Chinese names, so it never recognised any of the locales added since —
and a session whose title is not seen as a placeholder is never
auto-titled, so it keeps its default name forever.

It now walks `tray_i18n::ALL`, which already carries the same names for
the tray menu. `ALL` moves out of the test module to make that possible;
a second hand-kept roster would go stale the moment a locale is added.

Remote IM had its own two-entry copy that never even knew `zh-TW`; it
delegates now and keeps only its own "Remote IM" prefix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(remote-im): check the engine locale against the shipped roster

`engine_lang_follows_product_locale_not_hardcoded_zh` asserted
`matches!(lang, "en" | "zh" | "zh-TW")`, which was true when three
catalogs shipped. With fifteen, `app_locale()` resolves to whatever the
desktop asks for, so the assertion fails on any other language — and it
holds `APP_HOME_ENV_LOCK`, so that one panic poisons the lock and takes
the rest of the suite with it.

Measured on a Japanese desktop before this change: 37 failures, 36 of
them `PoisonError`. Green on an English CI runner either way.

fix(test): make cargo test parallel-safe again (#727)

* fix(test): take the shared app-home lock in plan_chrome

`GROK_APP_HOME` is process-global, and every other suite that repoints it
holds `paths::APP_HOME_ENV_LOCK` while it does. `plan_chrome::tests` used
a module-private `ENV_LOCK`, which serialises only this file — so under a
parallel `cargo test` it moved the app home out from under whichever
suite was holding the real lock.

The victim varies with timing: `plan_chrome`'s own round-trip loses its
saved chrome, or `integration_test::project_add_trust_remove_roundtrip`
reads a project list written to a different home.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test: tolerate a poisoned app-home lock

`APP_HOME_ENV_LOCK` guards a `()` — it serialises an environment variable,
so a panic under it leaves no invariant broken. But 38 of its acquisitions
were `.lock().unwrap()`, so one genuine failure turned into a wall of
`PoisonError` that buries the real one.

`with_isolated_project_store` and `store::tests` already did the
`unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())` dance; this makes it uniform.

fix(i18n): dates and clocks follow the chosen language (#729)

* fix(i18n): format list timestamps in the chosen locale

`PlanHistoryList`, `TraceHistoryList` and `MirrorConnectPanel` each carried a
byte-identical `toLocaleString(undefined, …)` helper, and the plan-history
preview in `AppWorkbench` inlined a fourth copy. `undefined` means "whatever
language the WebView reports", which is the OS language on some launch paths
and `en-US` on others — never the language the user picked in Settings. A
Japanese user reading a Japanese UI still got `Apr 15, 2026, 09:05`.

Replace all four with one `formatListTimestamp(iso, locale)` in
`src/lib/formatDateTime.ts`, built on the existing `intlLocale()` so `zh`
resolves to `zh-CN` rather than the macrolanguage. `locale` is a required prop
on the three components: making it optional would silently keep the old
behaviour for any call site that forgot it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(i18n): localize the quota reset clock

`formatQuotaResetTime` hand-built `MM-DD HH:mm`. That string is a date only to
a reader who already expects month first: a German user parses `04-15` as the
4th of month 15, and an en-US user never gets the am/pm their clock format
needs. It is shown in the sidebar account menu, the saved-account rows and the
account panel, so every locale but English-ish ones reads it wrong.

Take a `locale` and hand it to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, the same way
`formatRelativeTime` two functions above already does. `UserMenu` had no
locale at all, so it gains one from `AppWorkbench`; `AccountPanel` already had
one in scope.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(i18n): localize the tray quota reset clock

The tray usage row printed `MM-DD HH:mm` for every language. It is the only
place in the app that reads a date in a format its reader may not — a German
user sees `04-15` and has to guess whether that is April 15th or the 4th of
month 15.

Add `reset_time_fmt` to `TrayStrings` so the format travels with the rest of
the locale's tray copy, and have `format_reset_time` take it. `%p` appears
only for `en` and `fil`: chrono spells it "AM"/"PM" in English with no
localized form, so a 12-hour clock would be wrong everywhere else.

re-syncs and retries once.

changelog: 0.2.27

Move Unreleased notes into the 0.2.27 section for tagging.
chore: release v0.2.27

feat(ssh): add Settings Runtime SSH host list and connection probe

Read concrete Host aliases from ~/.ssh/config, test them via system OpenSSH
BatchMode, and probe remote Grok CLI plus login. Missing CLI or auth shows
copy-paste install and grok login --device-auth commands.

feat(ssh): watch hosts, live search, and remote folder picker

Split Settings SSH into Watching vs Available with a live filter.
Watching keeps an OpenSSH ControlMaster and scans remote Grok sessions
into the sidebar. New chats get a Remote chip to pick a watching host
and type or browse a remote path.

fix(ssh): align Settings SSH layout with settings-row padding

Section titles, search, and host rows now sit in .settings-row so copy
is not flush against the card edge. Sidebar remote sessions use the
tree rail inset instead of composer menu styles.

fix(ssh): make the watch switch flip immediately

Stop gating the Settings SSH watch toggle on a silent probe. Optimistic
checked state moves the host between Watching and Available; failures
revert and show an error instead of a no-op.

fix(ssh): quote ControlPath so watch works on macOS

macOS app data lives under Application Support. Unquoted
-o ControlPath=/Users/…/Application Support/… is parsed as a
ssh_config line and fails with extra arguments at end of line.

Quote values with spaces, keep mux sockets in the cache dir, and
lock both the OpenSSH argv (ssh -G) and the Settings switch click
path in tests so this class of bug does not need a screenshot.

fix(ssh): name remote sessions by host and first prompt

Sidebar remote list is grouped as Remote {alias}. Titles prefer a
custom name, then the first user sentence, then the cwd basename —
never the raw agent UUID. Full cwd is a hover tip. Newest 20 load
first with Load more. Click binds the SSH project and reports errors
instead of going silent. Double-click renames locally.

Remote context-menu parity with local sessions is deferred.

feat(ssh): open remote session transcripts in the chat pane

Clicking a watched remote session fetches chat_history.jsonl (or
updates.jsonl) over SSH, imports it into a local journal, and opens
that App session so the conversation is visible. Repeat clicks reuse
the same imported row and refresh the transcript.

fix(ssh): recover remote transcripts and show opening on the row

Python mixed print() with stdout.buffer.write() on a non-TTY SSH
pipe, so chat_history.jsonl landed before GROK_APP_HIST and the
parser saw an empty body. Verified against UTS session
01a01907-adf3-7e00-a7a8-aee1082b0556.

Flush stdout in order, accept jsonl emitted before the markers,
and put Opening / errors on the clicked row instead of below
the list.

fix(ssh): reuse local session rows and keep the chat rail in sync

Remote sessions now use tree-l2/tree-l3 + SidebarSessionName +
relative time instead of a custom rail. OverlayScroll listens to
native scroll so the thumb tracks fast wheel; MessageNodeRail
prefers mounted message rects so a tall imported answer does not
leave the tick in the middle.

Cmd/Ctrl multi-select delete stays a later TODO with the rest of
the remote context menu.

fix(ssh): group remote chats by path and marquee only overflow titles

Remote list is now 远程 {alias} → cwd folder → sessions. While a host
is watching, hide that host's sshAlias projects from the local tree
so the same chat is not listed twice.

Title marquee compares the real name-slot width instead of subtracting
a fake 78px action reserve, so short titles such as 2026-07-25-ICLR
do not scroll, and the animation stays clipped inside the name slot.

fix(ssh): skip local spawn and list only resumable grok sessions

Opening an imported remote transcript used the remote path as a local
cwd, so spawn ENOENT was shown as CLI_NOT_FOUND. SSH projects skip
local grok agent stdio until wave 3.

The remote sidebar listed every directory under ~/.grok/sessions.
On UTS 2026-07-25-ICLR that was 145 dirs vs 10 rows from
grok sessions list. Skip session_kind subagent / subagent_resume,
and skip empty shells that have only chat_history.jsonl with no
updates.jsonl and no title. Those cannot load.

feat(ssh): browse and save remote text files in Side Workbench

Wave 2: an sshAlias project lists, previews, and saves files over
OpenSSH instead of local std::fs. Relative paths cannot contain `..`.
Markdown and other UTF-8 text are previewable and writable up to 2 MiB.
The agent still does not spawn on the host.

feat(ssh): run Terminal, Skills, and localhost Browser on the remote host

Side Workbench Files already used OpenSSH. Terminal now spawns ssh -tt with
ControlMaster instead of local $SHELL, Skills lists remote grok inspect plus
project skills, and loopback URLs are forwarded with SSH -L so the embedded
webview hits the remote process rather than this machine.

feat(ssh): run grok agent stdio on the remote host

Wave 3: SSH projects spawn ssh -T with ControlMaster and exec grok in the
remote cwd. Imported chats keep the remote session id so ACP can resume.
Send and warm-connect are enabled; disconnect persistence is still Wave 4.

feat(ssh): new conversation from remote folder hover pencil

Remote cwd rows now use the same hover write control as local projects.
Clicking it registers that SSH path and opens a new chat in the remote cwd.

fix(ssh): pass grok ACP flags inside one remote script

OpenSSH joins the remote command into a single shell -c string. Extra argv
after bash -lc was not a real argument array, so grok never started and the
new remote chat exited as host_exit. Wrap cwd and grok flags as one script.

fix(ssh): never label a remote path as local CLI_NOT_FOUND

Warm-connect used the remote cwd as a local spawn directory when the
session had no ssh_alias yet. ENOENT was shown as "install Grok locally".
Resolve the alias from the connect arg, bound project, or path match;
missing local dirs fail as CONNECT_FAILED; re-bind project_id on import.

feat(chat): render LaTeX in markdown with KaTeX

fix(rewind): bound agent RPCs and block rewind on background mid-turn chats (#962)

Three defects in the rewind path, each with a sibling in the same file that
already did the right thing.

1. `rewind_drop_last_user_turn` awaited `rewind_execute_for` unbounded, twice
   on the fallback path. `AcpClient::request` allows 45s per method name and
   probes several, so the rollback dialog could spin for minutes. Both calls
   now share the 8s budget the sibling `rewind_to_prompt_index` already used,
   hoisted to `REWIND_AGENT_RPC_BUDGET`. A timeout skips the fallback index
   rather than spending a second budget on the stall the user already felt.

2. The fork child rewind ran after `with_handshake_budget` returned but while
   `connect_lock` was still held, so one fork pinned the global lock for the
   handshake plus the rewind probe chain and stalled every other chat's
   send/connect. It now uses `with_soft_rpc_budget`, which exists for exactly
   this ("soft-fail RPCs must not pin connect_lock").

3. `rewind_to_prompt_index` read busy state from the live slot only, so a chat
   demoted to background while streaming reported idle and the journal was
   truncated underneath the running turn. Extracted
   `rewind_blocked_by_running_turn`, which goes through `with_session_mut` to
   cover live and background, and uses `live_session_is_busy` so
   `prompt_in_flight` after an early `prompt_complete` still counts as busy.

Regression tests cover (3) in both directions; the mid-turn one fails on the
live-slot-only read.

fix(macos): keep main window key through launch so the first click lands

Cold launch can leave the main window non-key ~1s after show/page-load

Replace the old repair loop (which only ran when NSApp was inactive at

Also use the modern -[NSRunningApplication activateWithOptions:] instead
of tao's deprecated activateIgnoringOtherApps:, and log app_active in the
Focused handler so a resign-key from NSApp deactivation can be told apart
from a transient key steal.

perf(chat): memoize the full-journal scans in the transcript render body (#965)

`hasStreamingAssistant` and the live-tool guard scanned the whole journal from
the render body, so they ran on every ConversationThread render. The
virtualizer re-renders the thread on each window shift, which means a fling
paid three O(n) passes per frame on top of the mount and measure work.

- `hasStreamingAssistant` moves into a `useMemo` on `[messages]`.
- The two scans inlined in the JSX (`isToolInlinedInAssistants` plus a
  `messages.some` for an existing tool row) collapse into one `liveToolHasRow`
  memo on `[messages, liveTool]`. `liveTool` is itself a `useMemo`, so the
  identity is stable while scrolling.

Behaviour is unchanged: `!liveToolHasRow` is the same `!A && !B` predicate, and
the memo returns early when there is no live tool, which also skips the scans
entirely in the common case.

fix(ask-user): restore a pending questionnaire after a missed one-shot emit

`session://ask_user` is emitted once while the agent blocks on the
`_x.ai/ask_user_question` reverse RPC. Only the RPC id was stored, and there
was no restore command, so a WebView reload or window remount lost the
questionnaire for good: the chat sat at 「思考中」 with nothing to answer, and
the stall watchdog deliberately skips sessions holding an ask gate, so nothing
healed it. The permission card already had this recovery; ask-user did not.

Host: store the full payload as `pending_ask_user_ui` next to the rpc id,
mirroring `pending_permission_ui`, and add `pending_ask_user` /
`session_pending_ask_user` that gate the read on the rpc id — the field every
invalidation path already clears — so a resolved or recycled gate cannot
resurrect. Both emit sites now emit the stored struct itself, so a live event
and a restore cannot drift apart in shape.

Frontend: extract `restoreSessionGate` and use it for both gates in
`restoreForSession`. Sharing one helper is what keeps them symmetric; the
asymmetry is the whole bug. A restore never overwrites fresher state — it
re-checks the parked map before committing, so a live event always wins.

`UiAskUserRequest` uses the real `Option<String>` / `Vec<AskUserQuestionItem>`
types rather than `serde_json::Value`, and camelCase serialization keeps the
event payload byte-identical to the previous `json!` literal.

Net effect on the orchestration budget: App shell + AppWorkbench shrinks by one
line.

git_file_diff (git not-available probe + diff + untracked fallback),
git_review_bundle (5 spawns + numstat/patch parse), git_show_file

rename) all ran directly on the async runtime worker. The Review tab,

command. Same pattern as git_status (#990) and cli_worktrees_list:
fast path guards stay on the runtime, process spawns + disk writes go

perf(host): move worktree IPC commands onto the blocking pool (#992)

git_worktree_add materializes a full checkout (porcelain list, mkdir,

worktree from the UI froze every other queued IPC command for the
duration. Fast-path guards (path checks, sanitize, probe) stay on the
runtime; the spawns and disk walks go to spawn_blocking.

* perf(startup): slim boot critical path and vendor chunking

- viteManualChunks: isolate react/react-dom/scheduler into framework
  chunk so feature vendor chunks stop becoming static entry deps
  (root cause of tiptap 533KB being force-preloaded at boot)
- main.tsx: drop eager katex css, DEV-only scrollPerfDebug import
- markdownMath: load katex css on first markdown processor attach
- ProjectRulesModal / SideTabBody: lazy MarkdownTiptapEditor / TerminalTab
- OfficeDocumentPreview: split into pdf/docx/xlsx lazy sub-previews
- CodePreview: trim highlight.js registrations 68 -> 22 (preview falls
  back to plain text; codeLang map kept full for CodeMirror editor)
- delete dead ResourceViewer shell + 5 orphan modules (-4717 lines)
  and unused dompurify dependency

Fixes #1055

* perf(settings): lazy-load the settings tree out of the App chunk

WorkbenchSettingsStage is already gated behind settingsOpen — converting
to React.lazy moves the ~12k-line settings tree into an async chunk
(941KB) that only loads when the overlay opens.

App chunk 2,782KB -> 1,792KB raw (-36%), gzip 808 -> 572KB.

Fixes #1063

* perf(ui): stop per-token and per-hover render storms

Chat streaming path:
- standaloneToolGroups: structural-share the Map so transcript row memos
  are not busted by a fresh reference every stream flush (~10x/s)
- filterEchoedUserAttachments: return the input array when nothing was
  echoed (keeps AssistantMessageBody memo intact)
- MarkdownChat: memoize the stable-prefix ReactMarkdown tree so painted
  markdown is not re-parsed (and rehype-katex not re-run) every ~110ms
  tail flush
- useThoughtBodyFollow: drop followKey from the layout-effect deps —
  the ResizeObserver already follows growth; no more observer churn
  per token
- ConversationThread: liveTool memo comparison only fails the ACTIVE
  assistant row (it is the only place liveTool paints)

Non-chat surfaces:
- Heatmap: memoize day/week cells so hover setState no longer re-renders
  all ~371 buttons; selectRange now useCallback
- SshWatchProvider: 20s poll merges are identity-preserving when the
  fetched page is unchanged (no more forced consumer re-renders)
- WorkbenchSessionTree: group+sort sessions once per data change
  (useMemo) instead of O(projects x sessions) filter+sort per render

Fixes #1072

* fix: two WSL settings issues — blur re-probe and display path slash

fix: probe absolute WSL CLI paths via direct exec first (#1264)

The WSL CLI probe always ran through bash -lc, so detection depended
on the distro's login environment — bash on PATH, a quiet profile, a
set HOME. On distros where the login shell is noisy or minimal, an
installed CLI reported as not found even though a direct
wsl -d <distro> -- <cli> --version works.

Absolute wslCliPath values now probe with direct exec first (no
shell, no profile), and the bash -lc path stays as the fallback for
bare names, tilde paths, and any case where direct exec fails. The
spawn/wait/collect loop is shared between both probes.
